full_judgment:
2. The petitioners claim to have purchased an area of 283/4 decimals of land in Mouza Shamsharabad, Lakshmipur within the municipality appertaining to plot No. 1059 MRR Khatian No. 340 in the District of Lakshmipur from its recorded owners by registered kabala Nos. 10230-10231 dated 6-5-1984 and kabala Nos. 3786-3789 dated 20-3-1991. The petitioners after purchasing the aforesaid land constructed residential houses there in accordance with the approved plan after obtaining necessary permission from the local municipality and are residing there. In the meantime, beyond the know- ledge of the petitioners LA Case No. 34 of 1993- 1994 dated 5-4-1994 was started for the acquisition of an area of 1.46 acres of land including the petitioner's aforesaid land for extension of the Lakshmipur Sadar Hospital. Subsequently, it came to the knowledge of the petitioner that notices under sections 3 and 6 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 hereinafter "the Ordinance", was served upon the petitioner's predecessors-in-interest, the vendors of the land Lalit Mohan Pal and others in whose names the records of rights were prepared, fixing 9-7-1994 for objection hearing. The petitioners thereafter filed their objections with the Office of the Deputy Commissioner, Lakshmipur and although the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Lakshmipur made his award of compensation on 18-7- 1994 as per section 7(3) of the Ordinance, the petitioners have not received any compensation. On 10- 10-1995, the petitioner No. 1 filed an application with the Office of the Deputy Commissioner, Lakshmipur which was numbered as Petition No. 737 of 1995 giving rise to Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 1995-1996 praying for publishing a Gazette notification declaring abatement of the LA proceedings pursuant to section 12 of the Ordinance, for non- compliance of the provision of section 10 of the Ordinance, but the same was rejected by the respondent No.3, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Lakshmipur by the impugned order. The learned Advocate for the petitioner thereafter served a Notice of Demand for Justice to the respondents to publish a Gazette notification declaring abatement of LA Case No. 34 of 1993-1994 in respect of the land in possession of the petitioners but the respondent No.2 by his letter dated 24-4- 1996 refused to do so. Thereafter, the petitioner No. 3 was served with a notice on 23-4-1996 (Annexure-K) from the Office of the respondent No. 2 to vacate the aforesaid premises. 

 4. It is stated that the decision to acquire land by the aforesaid LA proceedings was finalised by the Deputy Commissioner, Lakshmipur on 12-6- 1994. Thereafter, the 'requiring body made the money available to the Deputy Commissioner on 8- 6-1995 for payment of compensation to the affected persons. The same was however, not paid to them and was deposited in the RD account on 2-3-1996 i.e. after one year and nine months. Thus compensation money having been deposited in the RD Account within one year of final decision of acquisition has resulted in a breach of section 10(2) of the Ordnance, and the Deputy Commissioner is required to make a Gazette notification that the acquisition proceedings have become abated. 

 5. The respondent No. I, Government of Bangladesh, is contesting the Rule by filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition and a Supplementary Affidavit denying the materiel allegations. It has been stated, inter alia, that LA Case No. 34 of 1993- 1994 was started on 12-6-1994 and all the steps were taken in accordance with law; It has been further stated that the compensation money was made available by the requiring body to the Deputy Commissioner on 8-6-1995 vide Memo No. 119(8) of the Ministry of Health and Family Planing which is well ahead of the statutory period of one year and that no question of abatement of the LA proceeding arises. It has been further stated that the land in question has already been handed over to the requiring body and that the petitioners cannot have any claim on it and that the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 6. Mr Mihir Kanti Majumder, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, had drawn our attention to the order sheet and records of LA Case No. 34 of 1993-1994 and submits that the Deputy Commissioner, Lakshmipur gave his final approval for acquisition of the petitioners' land on 6- 6-1994 and that the compensation money after being made available to the Deputy Commissioner's Office and after being offered to the affected persons was deposited in the RD Account on 2-3-1996 i.e. almost one year nine months after the final decision for acquisition of the petitioner's land was taken by the Government and therefore, the LA proceedings in respect of the petitioners' land will be deemed to have been abated and that in accordance with sections 10 and 12 of the Ordinance the Deputy Commissioner, Lakshmipur is required to make a declaration to that effect in the official Gazette. In support of his submission, the learned Advocate has drawn our attention to the decision in Bangladesh vs Subash Chandra Das and others reported in 46 DLR (AD) 63 as well as the decision in the case of Subash Chandra Das vs Bangladesh 50 DLR (AD) 106. 

 8. On perusal of the impugned order and the LA Case records it appears that the Deputy Commissioner, Lakshmipur gave final approval for acquisition of 1.46 acres, of land for the purpose of construction and extension of Lakshmipur Sadar Hospital on 6-6-1994. The respondent No. 1 with his Affidavit-in-Opposition and Supplementary Affidavit has annexed copies of the order sheet of LA Case No. 34 of 1993-1994 which shows that the Ministry of Health and Family Planning vide memo dated 119/1 (8) made available requisite funds to the Office of the Deputy Commissioner on 8-6-1995 for acquisition of land. Certified copy of the order sheet of the aforesaid LA Case annexed to the Writ Petition shows that notice to the affected persons for receiving compensation money was issued on 27-9- 1995; thereafter on 2-3-1996 order was passed for depositing unpaid compensation money in the RD Account maintained by the Office of the Deputy Commissioner, Lakshmipur. Thus it appears that money was deposited into the RD Account more than one year eight months after the final decision to acquire the concerned land by the Deputy Commissioner was taken. Section 10 of the Ordinance is as follows: 

 12. Abatement or revocation of acquisition proceeding: 

 (i) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Ordinance, where in any case the estimated amount of the award of compensation has not been deposited by the requiring person for acquisition of any property under section 5 within the period specified in section 7(4), all proceedings in respect of such acquisition shall, on the expiry of that period, stand abated and a declaration by the Deputy Commissioner to that effect shall be published in the official Gazette. 

 (2) The Deputy Commissioner may, with the prior approval of the Government, by notification in. the official Gazette, revoke all proceedings in respect of acquisition of any property at any time before the payment of compensation. 

 11. The aforesaid section of law provides that if compensation has not been paid or deposited within a period of one year from the date of decision of the Government of acquisition, proceedings in respect of acquisition shall stand abated and a declaration to that effect to be published in the official Gazette by the Deputy Commissioner. In the case of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration vs Subash Chandra Das & ors reported in 46 DLR (AD) 63, the Appellate Division held- 

 "The provision of section 12 will come into play only when the compensation is not paid or not kept in deposit account under section 1O(1). Under section 12 no obligation, as such, is placed on the requiring body to deposit compensation within six monthsfrorn the date of decision for acquisition." 

 "Compensation has not been paid or deposited within six months from the date of decision for acquisition in sub-section (1) of section 12 is to be understood with reference to section 10." 

 "An acquisition proceedings shall stand abated if compensation has not been paid or deposited within six months (now one year) from the date of the decision of the authority concerned for acquisition of the property." 

 14. Thus, from the aforesaid decisions it appears that the compensation money is to be deposited in the RD Account within one year of the decision failing which declaration has to be published in the official Gazette by the Deputy Commissioner that the acquisition property is abated. In the instant case, money was deposited after one year of taking final decision regarding acquisition proceeding. Thus, in our opinion, the whole proceeding is abated. 

 15. The learned Deputy Attorney-General has submitted that the, petitioner has no locus standi to file the instant writ petition. It appears that these petitioners are all from the same family as they seem to be the son or daughter or wife or husband of one another. It has been also stated that they purchased the' land by registered deeds from the persons who received notices under section 3 of the Ordinance for acquisition proceedings. (Annexure- C) Chairman, Municipality gave permission to the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 to construct a pucca building and homestead proposed to be acquisitioned. Annexure- K is a notice dated 23-4-1996 addressed to the petitioner No. 3 for vacating the concerned land. Thus, in our view, the petitioners have sufficient interest to file this Writ Petition and" therefore, the learned Deputy Attorney-General's submission that the petitioners have no locus standi is not acceptable. 

 16. The learned Deputy Attorney-General next submitted that the land has been acquired in LA Case No. 34 of 1993-1994 for public purpose for construction and extension of the Lakshmipur Sadar Hospital'. According to him, in view of the public interest the acquisition proceedings should not be disturbed. Although we are sympathetic to this submission nevertheless, it cannot be denied that the petitioners' right has been infringed and that a public functionary is required to perform his duties within the strict letter of the law. In the instant case, acquisition proceeding and award of compensation and its refusal ought to have been deposited in the public account within one year which has not been done. In such circumstances, the fact that the land has been acquired for a public benefit is not a sufficient excuse. In our opinion, if the respondents are interested in acquiring the petitioners' land for the public benefit then they ought to make fresh acquisition/requisition proceedings. The present acquisition proceedings of the petitioner's land appears to be hit by section 10 and 12 of the Ordinance. 

 17. We, therefore, direct the Deputy Commissioner, Lakshmipur to publish appropriate declara- tion in the official Gazette that the acquisition proceedings in LA Case No. 34 of 1993-1994, so far it relates to the petitioner's land comprising 28% decimals, stands abated.
